Greeting, I am Dr. Agent. You presented with gait and limb ataxia; to begin my assessment, how long have you been experiencing these balance and coordination difficulties?

Have you noticed any accompanying symptoms such as weakness, numbness, double vision, or changes in your speech?

speaker: Doctor
text: Good, the initial blood work and metabolic panel are normal. Since the basic metabolic causes have been ruled out, have you noticed any specific triggers for your ataxia, such as alcohol consumption, a specific medication, or recent trauma? Also, do you have a family history of similar balance issues?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned the clumsiness is worse on the right side; does this asymmetry suggest one specific limb is more affected than the other, or is it a generalized whole-body issue? Additionally, have you experienced any recent vomiting, nausea, or signs of head trauma?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: PML (Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy).

The combination of progressive gait and limb ataxia in a patient with Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab is highly suggestive of PML, a serious opportunistic infection of the white matter. I need to confirm the neurological progression and visualize the brain damage immediately.

REQUEST TEST: JC_Virus_Serology, MRI_Brain_with_contrast.
